description: Definitions for abstract argumentation: argumentation frameworks, conflict-freeness, admissibility, and semantics such as grounded, preferred and stable.
Definitions for bipolar argumentation: frameworks with attack and support, deductive and necessary support, coalitions and coalition-based semantics.
Definitions for abstract dialectical frameworks: acceptance conditions, three-valued interpretations, and semantics such as grounded, preferred and stable.
Definitions for incomplete argumentation: frameworks with uncertain arguments and attacks, completions, and possible and necessary acceptance.
Definitions for probabilistic argumentation: argument and attack probabilities, subframeworks, the constellation approach and acceptance probabilities.
Definitions for argumentation with collective attacks: range, weak defence, and semantics such as weak admissibility and weakly preferred.
Definitions for assumption-based argumentation: assumptions, contraries, inference rules, attacks, and semantics such as grounded, preferred and stable.
Overview tables for reasoning complexity: credulous and skeptical acceptance and verification for abstract argumentation and abstract dialectical frameworks.
Overview table for principles of argumentation semantics: which semantics satisfy reinstatement, directionality, SCC-recursiveness and more.
